title: Small bands versus big bands, and Walter Fuller's group
summary: Preferred big bands but liked Joe Kelly's; played with Fuller in Peoria on Pearl Harbor Day.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Do you prefer to play in small bands to big bands?

Not necessarily. It's hard to say I don't miss the big bands, because I'd be telling tales. I miss all that brass and saxophone, oh, no. But in a good band, like Joe Kelly's band, I enjoyed working with that band, because we'd sound like a big band. (Sound effect) Especially after Johnny Borg (PHONETIC) got in it. Oh, man, I'm telling you. So I, you know, I enjoyed working with Joe. But then I'm not saying I don't miss the big bands.
What was the last big band that you were with?

Dolgarn, I believe it was Earl. Because after Earl I went with Walker Fuller. That's right, I was with Walker Fuller. We had a small band, after Earl's band broke up. I stayed with Walker Fuller. I was with him about two, three years.

Walker Fuller, Omer Simeon -- I can't think of the guitar player's name. Roselle Claxton on piano. And Buddy Smith on drums. And I was on string bass. Yeah, we were together about two or three years. In fact, we was
Yeah, Walter -- Walter got pretty popular---he sang.
Yeah, he sang. He got real popular.
Did you make any records with him?
No, we never made any records.
When you were with Earl did you make any records, besides the ones you made with Earl?
All my recording was done with Earl while I was with him.
Did the band do any transcription dates?
No, we never got into that.
